summary.text: Eric Lucero is the Republican incumbent state senator for Minnesota State Senate District 30 and is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot for re-election against Democrat Leah Temple.

A cyber security specialist and former Dayton City Council member, he served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2015 to 2023 before moving to the Senate, and the Minnesota Senate's member directory lists him as a Republican representing District 30.

paragraphs.text: Eric Lucero lives in St. Michael, Minnesota, and graduated from Spring Lake Park High School.

He earned associate degrees in arts and in applied science in law enforcement from Century College, a B.S. in law enforcement and in computer forensics from Metro State University, and an M.B.A. from the University of Minnesota in 2010.
His career experience includes working as a small business owner, cyber security specialist, licensed real estate agent, licensed general contractor, college instructor and commercial truck driver.
Lucero served on the Dayton City Council and represented Minnesota House District 30B from 2015 to 2023, succeeding David FitzSimmons.
He was re-elected to the House in 2016, 2018 and 2020, and in 2022 he won Minnesota State Senate District 30, defeating Diane Nguyen with 65.2 percent of the vote in a race without an incumbent.
He assumed office in the Senate on January 3, 2023, succeeding Mary Kiffmeyer.
In 2025-2026 Lucero was assigned to the Education Finance Committee, the Elections Committee and the Housing and Homelessness Prevention Committee, where he is the ranking minority member.
His 2026 Republican primary was canceled, and Ballotpedia lists an endorsement from the National Federation of Independent Business (NFIB) Minnesota PAC.
